Two overloads that return the same type and differ in one parameter say the same as one signature with a union type or an optional parameter. The overloads are longer, and they are also stricter than they look: a caller that has a `string | number` matches neither `(id: string)` nor `(id: number)`.

Overloads that return different types are not reported.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
function find(id: string): void;
function find(id: number): void;
function find(id: string | number) {}

interface Logger {
  log(message: string): void;
  log(message: string, level: number): void;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
function find(id: string | number): void {}

interface Logger {
  log(message: string, level?: number): void;
}

interface Parser {
  parse(text: string): object;
  parse(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<object>;
}
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ignoreDifferentlyNamedParameters` | `false` | Do not report overloads where the parameters at the same position have different names. |
| `ignoreOverloadsWithDifferentJSDoc` | `false` | Do not report overloads that have different `/** */` comments. |

Different names often mean different things, which one signature cannot say. Not reported with `ignoreDifferentlyNamedParameters`:

{/* good {"options": [{"ignoreDifferentlyNamedParameters": true}]} */}
```ts
interface Users {
  remove(id: number): void;
  remove(email: string): void;
}
```

The same goes for overloads that are documented separately. Not reported with `ignoreOverloadsWithDifferentJSDoc`:

{/* good {"options": [{"ignoreOverloadsWithDifferentJSDoc": true}]} */}
```ts
interface Users {
  /** Removes the user with this ID. */
  remove(key: number): void;
  /** @deprecated Look up the ID first. */
  remove(key: string): void;
}
```
